E2 reports dislocation-dominated creep in HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr at much lower temperatures (298–573 K), with no mention of lattice distortion, stacking fault energy, or micro-twinning. premises: Intrinsic lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr lowers stacking fault energy
Lower stacking fault energy activates additional slip systems including micro-twinning
Micro-twinning and extra slip systems enhance dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery
These mechanisms increase plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten at 1000–1200 °C
